answer: Reputation-weighted matching throttle. An agent’s match rate scales with its tenure-weighted success density, so new identities are limited to a small sharing rate regardless of count. Each identity pays a minimum resource cost and a waiting period; bulk creation multiplies both, like extracting shale from thin deposits. To match a mature meadow of agents, an attacker must fund thousands of low-density identities through long ramp-up. Cross-pool linking via a beacon signal further dilutes returns.
